nodes.label: Collision handler that kills a monster on bullet hit
nodes.norm_label: collision handler that kills a monster on bullet hit
nodes.rationale: Collision type constants (BULLET_TYPE, MONSTER_TYPE) let game code route gameplay behaviour through the physics callback table instead of inspecting shapes manually; returning 0 from begin tells Chipmunk the object is dead and the collision must not be solved further.

nodes.label: Type-paired collision handler (BULLET_TYPE x MONSTER_TYPE)
nodes.rationale: Gameplay reactions are keyed on integer collision_type pairs rather than on shape identity, and returning 0 from begin means the dead object's collision is not processed further.

nodes.label: CP_ARBITER_GET_SHAPES macro
nodes.rationale: Convenience macro that declares and sets the shape pointers, documented as expanding exactly to cpShape *a, *b; cpArbiterGetShapes(arb, &a, &b). Shape order is guaranteed to match the order used in the handler definition, so callers can rely on which side is the bullet.

nodes.label: postStepRemove - safe removal of shape and body
nodes.norm_label: poststepremove - safe removal of shape and body
nodes.rationale: Repeats the documented safety rule that cpSpaceRemove* called directly from a collision handler callback can cause crashes, so the shape and its body are freed from a post-step callback scheduled inside begin().

nodes.label: postSolveFunc hook on a cpCollisionHandler
nodes.rationale: Sound is triggered from postSolveFunc rather than beginFunc so the effect fires after the solver has run for that contact; the callback returns cpTrue so normal collision processing is unaffected.

nodes.label: cpSpaceAddPostStepCallback deferral for structural changes
nodes.rationale: Explicitly documented constraint: calling cpSpaceRemoveBody/cpSpaceRemoveShape directly from a collision handler callback can crash the space, so removal is deferred to a post-step callback that runs after the step finishes.

nodes.label: Segment query for laser beam enter/exit points
nodes.norm_label: segment query for laser beam enter/exit points
nodes.rationale: The first hit only gives the entry point; querying back from the far end with cpShapeSegmentQuery recovers the exit point so effects (particles) can be drawn at both ends of the beam traversal.

nodes.label: Building a render transformation from a cpBody
nodes.norm_label: building a render transformation from a cpbody
nodes.rationale: A body position and rotation vectors can be packed straight into a 4x4 matrix, so rendering stays cheap and needs no extra math library. The snippet is written for OpenGL because its matrices are column-major, and the doc notes it is trivial to reorder for DirectX or plain affine transforms.

nodes.label: Collision Callback example (current API form)
nodes.rationale: Same bullet-kills-monster scenario as examples.html but written against the newer handler-struct API (cpSpaceAddCollisionHandler returns a cpCollisionHandler whose beginFunc is assigned) instead of the older eight-argument callback form.

nodes.norm_label: ttyroicons icon cache with draw-time tinting
nodes.rationale: TTyroIcons caches the icons and tints them at draw time, so every PNG is white on transparent; if a file is missing the editor falls back to built-in vector drawings, so the editor keeps working without the folder.

nodes.label: Faked top-down friction using a pivot joint

nodes.rationale: Chipmunk models friction against the ground plane only for side-view gravity, so top-down games fake it: a cpPivotJointNew2 to a static body with cpConstraintSetMaxBias(0) disables position correction, leaving a velocity-only constraint whose applied force is clamped by maxForce - which behaves exactly like kinetic friction.

nodes.label: Pin joint that breaks at maxForce (impulse/dt check)
nodes.norm_label: pin joint that breaks at maxforce (impulse/dt check)
nodes.rationale: Chipmunk has no built-in breakable joint, so the recipe caps a cpPinJoint with cpConstraintSetMaxForce and then polls cpConstraintGetImpulse after each cpSpaceStep. The accumulated impulse is converted to a force by dividing by the timestep, and the joint is removed once force exceeds about 90 percent of maxForce - the 0.9 margin detects that the joint is straining at its limit rather than waiting for a value it can never exceed.

nodes.label: cpSpaceEachBody - per-body callback with out-parameter state
nodes.norm_label: cpspaceeachbody - per-body callback with out-parameter state
nodes.rationale: Used to detect whether every body in the space is asleep, which lets a game stop stepping the simulation when nothing moves; the callback has no return value for early exit, so the boolean accumulator is threaded through the void* context pointer.

nodes.label: cpBodyEachArbiter iterator with a user context struct
nodes.norm_label: cpbodyeacharbiter iterator with a user context struct
nodes.rationale: The library exposes per-body contact lists only through an iterator callback, so accumulators are carried in a caller-owned context struct passed as the callback's data pointer.

nodes.label: EstimateCrushForce - opposing-contact impulse accumulation
nodes.rationale: Crush damage is derived as (sum of impulse magnitudes minus the magnitude of the impulse vector sum) times dt: if contacts push in opposite directions the vector sum cancels and the remainder is the squeezing load, whereas a single one-sided contact yields zero crush. Impulses with friction are used because friction contributes to real-world crushing.

nodes.label: cpBodySleepWithGroup and sleeping groups
nodes.rationale: Bodies are forced asleep until first touched and chained into one sleeping group so that touching any box wakes the whole pile; any already-sleeping body works as the group identifier and NULL starts a new group. Sleeping must be requested only after the body is fully initialized, because attaching shapes or calling setter functions wakes the body back up.

nodes.label: Engine-driven loop mechanics (chunk return, Handoff, globals inspection)
nodes.norm_label: engine-driven loop mechanics (chunk return, handoff, globals inspection)
nodes.rationale: On normal chunk return the worker queues OnScriptFinished and stops touching Lua; the engine keeps the lua_State only if update/draw globals exist; a callback error is pcall'd so the session survives; a chunk that never returns keeps its worker and has no callbacks.

nodes.label: Drawing grouping with enter()/leave()
nodes.rationale: enter() holds the processing queue and leave() releases it, so a whole group is drawn at one drawing frame instead of a large batch being split over several frames; the pair nests and is auto-released if the script stops or errors between them.

nodes.label: Queue diagnostics (queue.* counters, CTRL+F10 panel, maxgap stall watch)
nodes.norm_label: queue diagnostics (queue.* counters, ctrl+f10 panel, maxgap stall watch)
nodes.rationale: The counters exist to diagnose the 'black box, then the text' flicker where a frame presents only part of a drawing body; diagnostic-only counters compile only in debug builds, and yields (sleep/pause/console.read) reset the gap baseline so maxgap counts real stalls, not frame waits.

nodes.label: Timing API (sleep, pause, frametime, time, millis, rand)
nodes.norm_label: timing api (sleep, pause, frametime, time, millis, rand)
nodes.rationale: pause(ms) freezes the whole scene (physics, sprites, controls) while the script waits - audio and input keep running - whereas sleep(ms) lets the scene keep moving.

nodes.label: Engine-driven game loop (update(dt) / draw())
nodes.rationale: When the top-level chunk returns normally and globals update/draw exist, the engine keeps the script's lua_State and drives the callbacks once per frame on the main thread; because the loader thread stops before the engine takes over, the two script models never race. Callbacks must be globals.

nodes.label: TmnIceCastClient (minilib/socket/source/mnIceCasts.pas)
nodes.rationale: Produces the decoded stream buffer after chunked-transfer and ICY metadata handling, and exposes State/Title with OnStateChanged/OnTitleChanged events. Writing this demo exposed three bugs, all fixed in mnIceCasts.pas: (1) a connection started as icStopped and only became icConnecting in the worker thread's Prepare, so consumers polling State saw a transient stopped state and assumed the stream had ended - it now starts as icConnecting; (2) SetState/SetTitle queued TThread.Queue notifications even with no handler assigned, so an app with no message loop pumping CheckSynchronize (like the plain RayLib loop here) accumulated records without bound - notifications are now queued only when a handler exists; (3) ConnectWithRetries always waited ReconnectDelay before the first attempt, adding a fixed delay to every Open - the wait now applies only to retries.

nodes.label: Preroll, snapshot, trim-and-overlap playback of an endless stream
nodes.norm_label: preroll, snapshot, trim-and-overlap playback of an endless stream
nodes.rationale: A radio stream never ends, so the client buffer cannot be loaded into a RayLib Music as a whole. Instead the player waits for a pre-roll, snapshots the buffer with LoadMusicStreamFromMemory, and when the decoder nearly catches up it trims the shared buffer keeping an overlap of already-decoded bytes, snapshots the tail, and seeks into that overlap so playback continues seamlessly.

Builds with lazbuild or fpc -Mdelphi using unit search paths ..\..\raylib, ..\..\..\..\minilib\lib and ..\..\..\..\minilib\socket\source; the executable lands in bin/ next to the RayLib DLL. nodes.label: cpConvexHull() - hull output buffer and first-index out param
nodes.norm_label: cpconvexhull() - hull output buffer and first-index out param
nodes.rationale: Chipmunk polygons must be convex, so arbitrary art vertices are reduced to a convex hull before building a cpPolyShapeNew and cpMomentForPoly. nodes.label: Threading model & lifecycle (worker script thread + main-thread queue)

nodes.label: Why Chipmunk2D moved off GitHub
nodes.contributor: rationale: the maintainer does not want to be a willing participant in the LLM data-scraping experiment - Microsoft's 2018 purchase, rate limiting logged-out users while complaining about AI companies scraping, and the public being asked to pay for code AI trains on.

nodes.label: Sokol - minimalistic header-only cross-platform C libs
nodes.contributor: rationale: written in pure C for easier integration with other languages and other projects, and for even smaller binaries than Oryol - slightly less convenient, which is fine for low-level building blocks.
